previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, morbid obesity, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted with a dehisced right above-knee amputation stump and malodorous drainage. She had a history of Proteus mirabilis and Klebsiella pneumoniae infections, and outpatient imipenem was continued. Wound cultures during admission confirmed Proteus mirabilis and Enterococcus, with sensitivity to daptomycin, which was added before discharge. She underwent bedside debridements to promote healthy granulation tissue and received a vacuum-assisted closure device. Her dialysis schedule was maintained, and she was managed on Coumadin with heparin bridging. Hyponatremia was addressed with a 1.5 L fluid restriction. She remained afebrile with improving infection markers and was discharged to extended care for ongoing IV antibiotics, wound care, and rehabilitation.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ w/ hx of ESRD on HD (___), PAD s/p right 
AKA, DM, ___ p/w fevers, chills; HD catheter line insertion 
site noted to be purulent.

# Severe sepsis

Ms. ___ presented with an infected R IJ HD catheter site c/b 
S. aureus sepsis. Patient met SIRs criteria with fever, 
leukocytosis, and tachycardia upon admission. HD catheter 
inserton site was purulent and was removed on ___ after a 
session of dialysis. Blood cultures positive for S. aureus. She 
was started on vancomycin and meropenem for suspected skin 
source at catheter site and was given a line holiday. CXR 
unremarkable. Cultures returned sensitive to vancomycin. TTE did 
not show vegetations, although study quality was somewhat 
limited. Therefore, a TEE was conducted under anesthesia given 
the patient's apnea when previously exposed to the sedating 
medications required for the procedure. No vegetations were seen 
on TEE. A discussion was held with ___ and transplant surgery and 
it was determined that given her clot burden, vein stenosis, 
propensity to infection, and comorbid conditions, she is not a 
candidate for kidney transplant, fistula formation, or graft 
formation for dialysis. Peritoneal dialysis might be a viable 
option if she loses all remaining access. Therefore, a temporary 
L femoral line was placed on ___ and she continued to receive 
dialysis with vancomycin administration via HD protocol. On 
___, a venogram was performed in an attempt to re-cannulize 
her stenosed R IJ, but this attempt was unsuccessful and she 
received a tunneled L femoral HD catheter. Throughout her 
hospitalization, she was maintained on a low-potassium diet, 1.5 
L fluid restriction, and nephrocaps. She was discharged to 
receive HD at rehab with outpatient parenteral vancomycin 
therapy until ___. An ID follow-up appointment was scheduled.

#Abdominal pain/Constipation: During her hospitalization, Ms. 
___ frequently complained of abdominal pain. KUB negative. Her 
pain was always relieved after the administration of tap water 
enemas to induce bowel movements. Therefore, constipation was 
the most likely cause of her discomfort and a RUQ US was not 
necessary.

#Back pain: Ms. ___ complained of new back pain on ___. 
Given her S. aureus bacteremia, major concern was for epidural 
abscess vs osteomyelitis caused by endocarditis. Neuro exam 
reassuring, however, and patient did not have clear point 
tenderness on exam. ESR and CRP elevated as well as alk phos, 
but patient has previously had elevated alk phos. Her pain 
resolved over the next several days and TEE ultimately showed no 
vegetations.

L femoral line placed on ___ and tunneled L femoral 
catheter placed on ___. Given the number of invasive 
procedures she needed to undergo, her warfarin 2.5 mg daily was 
held and she was started on a heparin drip. Her normal ___ 
dialysis schedule was periodically altered to accommodate her 
procedures and line holidays. During her hospitalization, she 
was continued on cinacalcet and her sevelamer dose was titrated.

and currently has clots in numerous vessels from previous HD

COMPARISON:  Temporary dialysis line placement of ___.  

OPERATORS:  Dr. ___ (attending), Dr. ___ (fellow), Dr.

FLUOROSCOPY:  9 minutes, 100 mGy.

CONTRAST:  10 mL of IV Optiray contrast.

ANESTHESIA:  Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of
50 mcg of fentanyl throughout the total intra-service time of 55 minutes,
during which the patient hemodynamic parameters were continuously monitored by
an independently trained radiology nurse.  A total of 15 mL of 1% buffered
lidocaine was administered to the skin overlying the left internal jugular
vein and the left common femoral vein. 

PROCEDURE DETAIL: 

Informed consent was obtained outlining the risks and benefits of the proposed
procedure. The patient was brought to the angiography suite and positioned
supine on the imaging table. Ultrasound demonstrated no identifiable right
internal jugular vein. The left side of neck was prepped and draped in the
usual sterile fashion. A preprocedure timeout was performed as per ___
protocol. Following administration of 8 mL of 1% buffered lidocaine, the
compressible left internal jugular vein was accessed with a 21-gauge
micropuncture needle. A permanent ultrasound image was saved. A 0.018 inch
nitinol wire was unable to be advanced into the SVC.  A limited venogram using
5 mL of IV contrast demonstrated occlusion of the lower left internal jugular
vein.  The needle was removed.

Sonographic exam of the right groin demonstrated a very small caliber right
common femoral vein.  Sonographic examination of the left groin demonstrated a
patent and compressible left common femoral vein.  Following administration of
7 cmL of 1% buffered lidocaine, the left common femoral vein was accessed
using a micropuncture needle, taking care to avoid sites of infection and the
prior tunnel tract. A permanent ultrasound image was saved. A Nitinol wire was
advanced into the ___ and, after a skin incision was made, was exchanged for a
micropuncture sheath.  Brief venogram using 5 mL of IV contrast through the
micropuncture sheath demonstrated appropriate position in the left external
iliac vein.  Via the sheath, a short ___ wire was advanced into the IVC. The
subcutaneous tract was dilated using 10 and 12 ___ dilators. Again under
fluoroscopic guidance, a 20 cm, 13 ___ dialysis catheter with a VIP port
was advanced over the wire and the tip positioned in the left common iliac
vein. Excellent blood return was obtained from all lumens, and the catheter
was secured using a 0 silk suture. Sterile dressings were applied. The patient
tolerated the procedure well, and there were no immediate complications.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Placement of a 13 ___ temporary hemodialysis catheter with VIP port via
the left common femoral vein. The catheter tip lies in the left common iliac
vein and may be used for hemodialysis immediately.
2.  Central occlusion of left internal jugular vein.
3.  The right internal jugular vein and right femoral vein appear occluded as
well.

PELVIS

There is a left femoral large catheter in standard position.  No evidence of

Mild degenerative changes are in the distal lumbar spine.  Coarse dystrophic

degenerative changes in the left hip.

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Evaluation of the patient with end-stage renal
disease and recently placed femoral hemodialysis line, position.

AP radiograph of the pelvis was reviewed in comparison to ___.

The left femoral vein hemodialysis line terminates at the expected location of
the left iliac vein with its course being similar to the prior examination
obtained on ___.

Calcified fibroids are projecting over the pelvis.  No other abnormalities
demonstrated.

HISTORY:  ___ year-old woman with temporary left groin hemodialysis line. 
Request conversion to a tunneled line.

COMPARISON:  ___.

CLINICIANS:  Dr. ___, Dr. ___, Dr. ___ Dr. ___
(fellow).  The attending was present throughout the entirety of the procedure.


ANESTHESIA:  General anesthesia was used for the entirety of the case.

TASKS:
1.  Attempted right internal jugular venous access including an attempt to
place a snare in the remnant IJ via the left groin access.
2.  Over the wire change of left temporary groin HD catheter to tunneled HD
catheter.

TECHNIQUE/FINDINGS:

The procedure was discussed in detail with the patient and risks and benefits
emphasized.  Informed written consent was obtained. 

When the patient arrived in the angiography suite, general anesthesia was
induced and she was positioned supine on the procedure table.  Both upper
chest and neck in addition to the left groin were prepped and draped in usual
sterile fashion.  A preprocedural time out was performed per ___ protocol.

Ultrasound and fluoroscopy imaging was used an attempts to recanalize the
right internal jugular vein.  Multiple techniques were attempted including
using a snare from the left groin access and percutaneous access and
opacification of a right neck collateral without success. For the snare
attempt, a 5 ___ vertebral catheter was advanced over a 0.035 inch
Glidewire from the sheath in the left groin into the right internal jugular
vein. Contrast injection opacified collateral veins in the right neck. The
Glidewire was exchanged for a 20 mm gooseneck snare, but the snare could not
be positioned cephalad enough to allow visualization under ultrasound or
percutanous access. A collateral vein in the right lateral neck/chest was
accessed under ultrasound guidance using micropuncture technique. A permanent
ultrasound image was saved to PACS. The contrast injection via the
micropuncture sheath demonstrated flow to the right brachiocephalic vein via
collaterals, but the wire could not be passed centrally. 

After multiple attempts, we decided to terminate those attempts and our
attention was focused on the left groin.  After instillation of lidocaine with
epinephrine, a 51 cm cuffed dialysis catheter was tunneled from the left more
laterally to the site of the sheath in the left femoral vein. At this time,
the sheath which had been exchanged for the temporary left-sided groin HD
catheter was exchanged for a peel-away sheath, and the dialysis catheter was
placed through the sheath.  Supine fluoroscopy confirmed position of the tip
of the catheter in the IVC. Both lumens flushed without difficulty.

The catheter was secured to the skin using silk stitches.  The venotomy site
was closed using a subcutaneous ___ Vicryl stitch.  The patient left the
department in stable condition.  There were no immediate complications.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Unsuccessful attempts to access the right internal jugular vein.
2.  Over the wire change of a temporary left-sided groin HD catheter for a
tunneled HD catheter. The tip lies in the IVC. The line is ready for use.

HISTORY:  ___ female status post recent placement of a tunneled
hemodialysis catheter within the left groin, now presenting with left thigh
pain and falling hematocrit.  Assess for hematoma.

COMPARISON:  Fluoroscopic images from ___, and concurrent
abdominal radiograph performed immediately after the ultrasound.

LEFT GROIN ULTRASOUND:  No hematoma is identified in the region of recent
catheter placement.  The tunneled portion of the catheter is seen within the
superficial subcutaneous tissues, though its course cannot be followed more
proximally to the junction of the common femoral vein, due to technical
factors.  However, the catheter is confirmed to be in the expected position on
subsequent radiographs.  The left common femoral vein and artery are patent. 
No pseudoaneurysm is identified.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No hematoma at site of recent line insertion in the left groin.

2.  Catheter position could not be seen on ultrasound, though appropriate
position was confirmed on concurrent abdominal radiograph.

3.  No evidence of pseudoaneurysm.

p.m. on ___ by telephone.

INDICATION:  ___ female with recent placement of a tunneled left
hemodialysis catheter with incomplete evaluation of the catheter course on
recent left groin ultrasound.  Radiograph for confirmation of catheter
position.

COMPARISON:  Abdominal radiograph from ___ and fluoroscopic
imagines from ___.  

SUPINE ABDOMINAL RADIOGRAPH, FOUR IMAGES:  A tunneled hemodialysis catheter
projects over the left pelvic brim, crosses midline, and terminates with the
tip in the expected position of the upper IVC.  Findings are similar to
post-procedural fluoroscopic images taken on ___.  There is a
nonspecific bowel gas pattern without evidence of obstruction.  Calcified
fibroids are identified within the pelvic inlet.  Imaged lung bases are clear.

IMPRESSION:  Tunneled left femoral hemodialysis catheter within expected
unchanged position, terminating in the IVC.

HISTORY:  ___ woman with ESRD on multiple infections with oozing
catheter site and concern for hematomas versus infection.  

COMPARISON:  Recent ultrasound Doppler study from ___.  

FINDINGS:

A catheter is identified in the left femoral region, demonstrating posterior
shadowing.  No hematoma or collection is identified in the region of recent
catheter placement. There is some subcutaneous edema, but no evidence of fluid
collections. Tunnel portion of the catheter is again identified within the
superficial subcutaneous tissues.  

IMPRESSION:

Subcutaneous edema, but no evidence of fluid collections to suggest hematoma
or abscess.
